title: NGC 346 (NIRCam Image)
caption: Star cluster NGC 346 and its nebula, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 346 · constellation Tucana · about 200,000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: NASA Webb image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Arcs of orange and pink gas curve through the center of the frame in a boat-like shape, and another plume of the same colors spreads outward. Webb's Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) captured NGC 346, a star cluster inside a nebula 200,000 light-years away in the Small Magellanic Cloud, a nearby dwarf galaxy.

The colors trace two kinds of hydrogen. Pink marks energized hydrogen, typically at around 10,000 °C or more. Orange marks dense, cold molecular hydrogen at around -200 °C or less, along with dust. Stars form in that colder gas and then reshape their surroundings, as their light breaks down dense clouds into ridges and glowing pillars.

The Small Magellanic Cloud holds fewer elements heavier than hydrogen and helium than our galaxy does, so scientists expected little dust there. Webb found the reverse. For the first time it detected dust, as well as gas, in the disks feeding young protostars in NGC 346, building material for stars and possibly planets.
scale: NASA lists this view as about 3.9 arcminutes across, roughly 240 light-years at the object’s distance.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam captured this near-infrared view. NASA shows F444W in red, F335M in orange, F277W in cyan and F200W in blue.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, so the pink and orange are colors assigned to filters, not the gas's own hues.

explore: Conditions in the Small Magellanic Cloud resemble those of 'cosmic noon', the era when star formation in the universe peaked. Earlier infrared studies focused on protostars of more than about 5 to 8 solar masses, but Webb reaches down to protostars of about one tenth of the Sun's mass. The team suggests rocky planets might have formed earlier in the universe than once thought.
